Andrés Bello was a Venezuelan-born scholar, poet and lawyer who spent his later life in Chile. He wrote its Civil Code and founded its national university.

Born in Caracas, he taught the young Simón Bolívar and went with him to London in 1810, where he stayed for nineteen years. In 1829 he moved to Chile, where he served the government, drafted its foreign policy and became the first rector of the University of Chile in 1843.

His Civil Code of 1855 was copied by many Latin American countries, among them Ecuador and Colombia. His Spanish grammar of 1847, written for Americans, helped keep the language united after independence. He stands with Santiago's builders as a founder of the Chilean state.
sum: Andrés Bello was a Venezuelan-born scholar, poet and lawyer who spent his later life in Chile. He wrote its Civil Code and founded its national university.
